resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR calls it Maple Lake; Tennessee Landforms, the 2014 National Register list and OpenStreetMap call it Maple Creek. The Carroll County location and coordinates within a few meters match, so the sources are treated as describing one tower
NHLR gives 726 ft (221 m) and Tennessee Landforms gives 711 ft; elevation is not used in the story

notes_for_editor: The name and build-date issues are the main risk: the build date is only a lower bound from the badge outline, and the name conflict is resolved by location, not by a source that uses both names. Do not confuse this with the Natchez Trace Fire Tower (US 1716), a separate tower in the same state forest area that the Register describes as a 70-foot International Derrick tower built by the CCC in 1937; that description came from a search snippet and was not fetched, and it is not used here. No source read says who staffed the tower or whether it has public access.
